slides.label: DRG
slides.caption: A sensory ganglion: the first step in sensing, where a physical stimulus becomes spikes bound for the cord.

slides.label: sciatic
slides.caption: Myelinated axons in cross-section; fiber diameter and myelin set how fast each one conducts.

slides.label: TRP ISH
slides.caption: Only subsets of DRG neurons carry TRP channels — the detectors for heat and chemical irritants.

slides.label: Piezo2 ISH
slides.caption: Piezo2 marks mechanosensory neurons; Calca marks peptidergic ones — different cells, different jobs.

slides.label: DRG L4
slides.caption: Large NF200+ neurons and small peptidergic CGRP+ neurons share one ganglion.

sources.citation: Usoskin D et al., 2015, Nat Neurosci

slides.label: thalamus
slides.caption: The ascending somatosensory relay: thalamus (VPL/VPM) hands off to primary cortex (SSp).

slides.label: brainstem
slides.caption: Vagal interoceptive afferents end in the NTS, beside the area postrema — the brain's visceral inbox.

slides.label: islet
slides.caption: Extrinsic afferents sense internal organs like the pancreas — endocrine islet set in exocrine acini.

paper.citation: Brissova M et al., 2005, J Histochem Cytochem

slides.label: Fos ISH
slides.caption: After inflammation, c-Fos marks activated TRPV1+ nociceptors — a snapshot of sensitization.

slides.label: DRG atlas
slides.caption: Molecular markers split DRG neurons into subtypes — the transcriptomic map the field now builds on.

slides.label: innate ISH
slides.caption: Innate first responders, read by marker mRNA: myeloid cells (Lyz2) and neutrophils (S100a8).

paper.citation: Wallrapp A & Chiu IM, 2024, Annu Rev Immunol

slides.label: T/B ISH
slides.caption: The adaptive lymphocytes side by side: T cells (Cd3e) and B cells (Cd19).

paper.citation: Wallrapp A & Chiu IM, 2024, Annu Rev Immunol

slides.label: cytokine ISH
slides.caption: Cells caught making pro-inflammatory cytokines — the immune system's short-range signals.

paper.citation: Wallrapp A & Chiu IM, 2024, Annu Rev Immunol

slides.label: cortex Iba1
slides.caption: Iba1+ microglia tiling the cortex, each surveying its own territory.

slides.label: cortex GFAP
slides.caption: Resting cortex: sparse GFAP+ astrocytes among NeuN+ neurons — the baseline you compare neuroinflammation against.

slides.label: CGRP axis
slides.caption: A neuron-to-immune signal: nociceptor CGRP (Calca) acting on RAMP1+ target cells.

slides.label: DRG cyto-R
slides.caption: Sensory neurons carry cytokine receptors (Il6ra, Tnfrsf1a), so immune signals can change their firing.

paper.citation: Wallrapp A & Chiu IM, 2024, Annu Rev Immunol

slides.label: gut wall
slides.caption: CGRP+ sensory fibers run up the lamina propria to the epithelium and along the gut muscle, with CD45+ immune cells clustered beside them — the sensory and immune sides of the gut wall in one section.

slides.label: brainstem
slides.caption: The vagal inflammatory reflex hub: sensory NTS beside the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus (DMX).

slides.label: control
slides.caption: Every stain needs controls: a positive tissue proves it can work, a secondary-only slide catches false signal.

slides.label: Cre ISH
slides.caption: A Cre reporter reads out genetics: the tdTomato transgene appears only in Bmpr1b-lineage cells.

slides.label: intersect
slides.caption: Two driver genes rarely mark the same DRG neuron; the few that express both are exactly what an intersection targets.

slides.label: retro ISH
slides.caption: A retrograde AAV from an organ labels (tdTomato) the DRG neurons that innervate it.

slides.label: DREADD ISH
slides.caption: A manipulation check: c-Fos rises in hM3Dq-expressing neurons after the actuator, confirming they fired.

slides.label: cord
slides.caption: Good perfusion, fixation and sectioning are what give clean, interpretable morphology.

slides.label: cortex IF
slides.caption: Primary and secondary antibodies label specific proteins (NeuN, GFAP); DAPI marks every nucleus.

slides.label: RNAscope
slides.caption: Probe-based single-molecule dots show exactly which cells express a gene.

paper.citation: Usoskin D et al., 2015, Nat Neurosci

slides.label: confocal
slides.caption: Confocal microscopy resolves fine microglial processes — the basis for honest quantification.

slides.label: reference
slides.caption: Measuring RNA needs reference genes (Actb, Gapdh) to normalize against.

paper.citation: Usoskin D et al., 2015, Nat Neurosci

slides.label: DRG
slides.caption: An intact sensory ganglion — the tissue you dissociate to image live DRG neurons.

slides.label: scRNAseq
slides.caption: Sequencing defines clusters; in-situ probes (Sstr2, Adra2a) validate them back in the tissue.

paper.citation: Usoskin D et al., 2015, Nat Neurosci

slides.label: brain
slides.caption: The CNS, shown here as brain (cortex and hippocampus); the PNS lies everywhere outside it.

slides.label: autonomic
slides.caption: Central autonomic command in the hypothalamus: the paraventricular nucleus (PVH).

slides.label: cord L4
slides.caption: Transverse cord: the dorsal horn takes sensory input, the ventral horn sends motor output.

slides.label: sciatic
slides.caption: A peripheral nerve bundles fast myelinated and slow unmyelinated axons together in fascicles.

slides.label: DRG
slides.caption: One ganglion, two worlds: the DRG carries both somatic and visceral afferents to the cord.

slides.label: islet
slides.caption: Two organs in one: an endocrine islet set within the exocrine, enzyme-making acini.

paper.citation: Brissova M et al., 2005, J Histochem Cytochem

slides.label: islet α/β
slides.caption: The islet sets blood glucose: β cells make insulin, α cells make glucagon.

paper.citation: Brissova M et al., 2005, J Histochem Cytochem

slides.label: reflex arc
slides.caption: The spinal cord closes the reflex arc — sensory in through the dorsal root, motor out through the ventral.

slides.label: pancreas DRG
slides.caption: Your project in one slide: retrogradely-labeled, DREADD-bearing pancreas-innervating DRG neurons.
